einstellungen.text: Your bus driver is standing at the edge of the dam. And Paul is waving.
You only see him in the window. Tiny next to Henrik, his schoolbag on his back.
Paul holds out his old ticket to Henrik.
Henrik pulls his stamp out of his jacket. His hands shake so hard, he has to try twice.
Click. Twelve twelve, Millbrook Lane. Stamped. After twenty-eight years.
“I'm sorry I didn't stop for you.”
Paul turns around and walks into the fog. Toward the water. Toward the village.
His wet footprints go all the way to the edge. And there, they just stop.
Twelve thirty-one. The sign is back to normal. Outside, streetlights glow.
Henrik drives you all the way to your front door. Neither of you says a word.
In the morning, your mom hugs you. For a long time. She doesn't ask.
Your grandpa is at the breakfast table. You say just two words: Paul. Millbrook.
Your grandpa sets down his coffee. Paul was his neighbor's kid. No one has seen him since that night.
You reach into your jacket pocket. Your ticket from last night.
There's a stamp on it you never got. Millbrook Lane, twelve twelve. Round trip.
